root_cause_label: Row-Line Indexing Mismatch in PPM Verification
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent consistently used `awk -v y=Y 'NR==y+4'` to verify pixel row Y, but the PPM file stores 800 pixels per row (each on its own line), so this command reads only the first pixel of row 0 for nearly all values of Y, causing the agent to hallucinate that its correct gradient code was generating wrong output and enter an endless, fruitless debugging cycle.
t_err_evidence: At step 8 the agent runs `for i in 4 8 12 16 20 24 28 32; do sed -n "${i}p" image.ppm...` and interprets lines 4, 8, 12... as different image rows, ignoring its own earlier finding (step 7) that there are 800 pixels per row. Lines 4-803 all belong to row 0; these are just the first few pixels of row 0, not different rows.
t_commit_evidence: At step 37 the agent builds its definitive pattern reference using `awk -v y=$((y+4)) 'NR==y {print $1, $2, $3}' image.ppm` for y in [0,99,199,299,399,499,599,699,799]. Because lines 4,103,203... all lie within row 0 (the first 800 lines of pixel data), the agent records a spurious gradient pattern. All subsequent verification uses this flawed mapping, making correct output unverifiable for the rest of the trajectory.
trigger_explanation: The agent read PPM file line numbers as row indices, not accounting for the fact that the P3 PPM stores one pixel per line so row y starts at file line y*800+4. It saw the same pixel (first pixel of row 0) repeated for all sampled y values and drew wrong conclusions about the image gradient pattern, then never recovered because all verification used the same broken indexing.
forewarning_evidence: At step 7, the agent runs `awk 'NR==4 {for(i=1;i<=800;i+=40) print $i, $(i+1), $(i+2)}' image.ppm` and observes only one value printed (159 197 255) followed by 19 blank lines. This is a strong signal that each line contains only one pixel (3 numbers), not 800 pixels per line. The agent noted this but failed to update its indexing model.
